title: Probe-driven quality halt for staged model promotions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see subtle regressions surface only after a small fraction of production traffic is exposed to a new model variant. Existing canary heuristics are tied to simple aggregate throughput/latency/error metrics and miss semantic degradations that matter for customers (hallucination rate on instruction prompts, embedding divergence for search reranks, policy classifier drift).

Goal: Implement a probe-driven promotion halt that 1) monitors model quality against curated probe buckets (representative prompt slices) during staged promotions (shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%); 2) computes lightweight per-bucket scorecards with configurable acceptance windows and hysteresis; and 3) automatically pauses/promotes rollback to a safety tier when scorecards breach thresholds. The feature must work with both shadow and split experiments and integrate with existing rollout conductor.

Scope: MVP to cover text-generation APIs (chat/generation) and embedding endpoints. Key components:
- Probe bucket definition format (JSON schema) that can be attached per-customer or global. Buckets include prompt examples, expected token-level invariants, and a weighting.
- Streaming probe evaluator service that scores live responses against expectations (similarity, coverage, toxicity signal, token budget regressions).
- Scorecard aggregator with decayed rolling window and confidence intervals (to avoid flapping on small sample sizes).
- Promotion control hook in rollout conductor to pause advancement or trigger autorestore to baseline model.
- Dashboard and alerting (Console) with per-bucket charts and suggested mitigation actions.

Non-goals: Full human-in-the-loop adjudication workflow for the MVP (we will add later). Automated content-label remediation is out of scope for now.

Design decisions / tradeoffs considered: 
- Where to run evaluation logic? We will run lightweight heuristics in the control plane (streaming service) to keep serving path untouched; heavy evaluations (annotator-based) will run asynchronously and enrich scorecards. This balances latency and safety.
- Thresholding: use Bayesian credible intervals on metric deltas (rather than fixed counts) to reduce false positives on low-volume probes.
- Data locality: support both hosted and Dedicated in MVP by having a deployment variant for the evaluator service that can be co-located in customer VPCs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Rollout conductor can automatically pause promotion when any probe bucket shows degradation exceeding configured delta with >=95% posterior probability in the last 15 minutes.
- End-to-end test harness simulates degradations and verifies conductor pauses, and rollback path restores baseline model within configured SLO.
- Console shows per-bucket charts with sample failing prompts and links to adjudication doc.
- Performance: evaluator adds <2ms median added control-plane latency per request and scales to 5k concurrent model streams.

Open questions:
- Probe bucket ownership model: per-customer vs global curated. Proposal: MVP supports global and tenant-curated buckets; enforced via RBAC for private deployments.
- How to present uncertainty to PMs/Design (UI language around "probable regression" vs "confirmed").

Related artifacts: 
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ML/Probe+Driven+Promotion+Halt (draft)
- Proposal PR (internal GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3248
- Dashboard mockups (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/Probe-Scorecards

Dependencies: ["ENG-52011", "ENG-741205"]

Risks and mitigation: 
- False positive pauses on low-volume buckets: mitigate with min-sample thresholds and credible intervals; allow manual override.
- Performance overhead in control plane: perform staged rollout of evaluator, include canary for heavy customers.

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Finalize probe bucket JSON schema and validation (owner: Marcus).
2) Implement streaming evaluator skeleton and local test harness (owner: Marcus + Lina Gomez).
3) Integrate pause hook with rollout conductor and add unit/e2e tests (owner: Marcus + SRE).
4) Create Console surface for showing probe hits and suggestion actions (PM: Daniel Ruiz, Design: Priya Shah).

Estimated timeline: 2 sprints (design + implementation + e2e).

notes: This ticket focuses on making staged promotions safer by elevating semantically meaningful regressions into automated promotion controls. Coordinate with SRE for capacity testing and with Legal for PII handling in probe examples.
